results.title: Nutrifoods Ghana named confectionery company of the year at 6th Chamber Business Awards
results.content: Nutrifoods Ghana Limited, a leading manufacturer of snacks and culinary products in Ghana’s fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) sector, has been named Confectionery Company of the Year at the 6th Ghana National Chamber of Commerce and Industry (GNCCI) Chamber Business Awards, in recognition of its commitment to manufacturing excellence, innovation, product quality and contribution to Ghana’s industrial development. results.title: Global hegemons and the discussion for peace: Negative peace, positive peace or economic peace?
results.content: The three world leaders, President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin, on November 19, 2026, held a maiden edition of a tripartite engagement ostensibly to talk about peace. With the leaders declaring peace, will it be just a rhetoric or reality? Will these world leaders see to it that the negative peace concept is realized? results.title: Suspect linked to seven rape and robbery cases dies during Kade police operation
results.content: The Ghana Police Service has linked a 39-year-old ex-convict, Kwaku Asomani, to seven cases of robbery and rape, as well as the murder of a 28-year-old woman in Kade and surrounding communities in the Kwaebibirem District of the Eastern Region.

results.title: Remove Larabanga Mosque from new GH¢2 note, they’re intolerant of other religions – Christian group tells BoG
results.content: A Christian advocacy group, the Alliance of Christian Apologists, Ghana, has asked Government and the Bank of Ghana (BoG) to take the Larabanga Mosque off the new GH¢2 banknote before the Heritage Series notes go into circulation on December 1, 2026. The group says it accepts the mosque as an important Islamic heritage site. Its objection is to the mosque being presented on the national currency as a symbol of religious tolerance and diversity. It argues that the history of the Larabanga community contradicts that message. "Religious heritage is not the same thing as religious tolerance," the Alliance said in a press statement dated November 16, 2026.

results.title: Education Ministry says early BECE directive will not disadvantage gifted learners
results.content: The Ministry of Education says its directive restricting Junior High School (JHS) 1 and 2 students from registering for the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) is not intended to discourage gifted learners or limit their academic potential.

results.title: Police link ex-convict shot dead in Kade to seven rape and robbery cases
results.content: The Eastern South Regional Police Command says a 39-year-old ex-convict, Kwaku Asomani, who died during a police operation in Kade, has been linked to seven incidents of robbery and rape, as well as the murder of a 28-year-old woman. In a statement issued on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, and signed by DSP David Fianko-Okyere of the Public Affairs Unit, the police said preliminary investigations linked the suspect to incidents recorded between February 19 and November 10, 2026. According to the police, the suspect robbed female victims aged between 18 and 54 of money and personal belongings before sexually assaulting them. "The suspect robbed his victims, aged between 18 and 54, of various sums of money and personal belongings, and also sexually assaulted them," the statement said.

results.title: NHIS coverage rises from 57% to 70% in less than two years – Akandoh
results.content: Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh says coverage under Ghana's National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) has increased from 57% in 2024 to 70% in less than two years. Contributing to the 2027 Budget debate in Parliament on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, Mr Akandoh said the government had taken steps to strengthen the scheme and improve access to healthcare. "In 2024, the coverage of the National Health Insurance stood at 57%. In less than two years, the National Health Insurance has now hit 70%," he told Parliament.
